userStories.title: The koda connection and the flow input
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the flow module's connection selector and strict input parser without changing existing production files.

**Motivation** — The user wants one brainstorm to turn into ready PRs with as little of their attention as possible.

**Approach** — Credential and connection (my call, departs from the source design):

The source design proposed a new `nax auth login koda` credential kind. This spec instead reuses the koda
connection nax already has: `memory.koda.url` (koda's API root including its `/api` prefix) and
`memory.koda.headers` (the literal `Authorization: Bearer <agent key>` header). Reasons, from the code:

- Both keys are already global-only (`KODA_GLOBAL_ONLY_KEYS` in `packages/nax/src/config/global-only-keys.ts`),
  so a repository's `.nax/config.json` cannot point the key at another server.
- Header values are carried literally, with no `${VAR}` expansion (`LITERAL_SUBTREE_PATHS` in
  `packages/nax/src/config/dotenv.ts`), and `koda-http.ts` redacts them from every error.
- The `nax auth` store is built for LLM providers: `StoredCredential` is a closed union of `api-key` and
  `oauth`, `nax auth login` resolves the provider against pi's catalog, and unknown kinds are coerced to
  `api-key`. A non-LLM kind would touch three packages for a key nax already stores once.
- One koda, one agent key: a second home for the same key could drift from the first.

The connection is present when `memory.koda.url` is set and `memory.koda.headers` has an `authorization`
header (matched case-insensitively) with a non-empty value. `memory.enabled`, `memory.provider` and
`memory.koda.project` play no part: koda resolves the repository from the remote URL.

The request:

Tool input (JSON schema, `additionalProperties: false`):

```json
{
  "features": [
    { "feature": "nax-flow-send", "specPath": ".nax/features/nax-flow-send/spec.md" },
    { "feature": "nax-flow-docs", "specPath": ".nax/features/nax-flow-docs/spec.md", "dependsOn": ["nax-flow-send"] }
  ],
  "roles": { "reviewer": "acp:codex", "supervisor": "acp:claude" },
  "costCapUsd": 5
}
```

nax checks the input before the card, mirroring the koda checks that are cheap to repeat, so a bad request
fails before anything is pushed (koda stays the authority and re-checks everything):

- `features` has 1 to 20 entries; each `feature` matches `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{0,127}$`; names are unique.
- each `specPath` is 1 to 300 characters, ends in `.md`, does not start with `/`, contains no NUL character
  and has no `..` segment.
- each `dependsOn` entry names a feature that appears earlier in the list, never itself, and appears once.
- `roles.reviewer` and `roles.supervisor` each match `^[A-Za-z0-9._:/\[\]=,-]{1,200}$`. They are model
  strings koda passes to its review steps (for example `acp:codex`), not nax alias names; nax does not
  resolve `agent.modelAliases` (my call: koda's runner resolves models on its own machine).
- `costCapUsd` is a JSON number (a numeric string is rejected, my call) greater than 0 and at most 1000 whose
  `String()` form matches `^\d+(\.\d{1,4})?$`, as koda tests it.
- the input has no keys beyond `features`, `roles` and `costCapUsd`, and `features` is an array.

nax checks and sends each `specPath` exactly as given; koda normalises it on its side.

**Scope** — In: Create `packages/nax/src/chat/flow/` with a barrel, `flow-input.ts` and input types, and `flow-connection.ts`; add unit tests for the selectors and parser. Out: Repository/git checks and HTTP creation belong to US-002; the tool, JSON schema exposure, card and prompt belong to US-003; provider availability in chat belongs to US-004. A new `koda` credential kind in the `nax auth` store, and `nax auth login koda`, are not part of this feature; the connection is `memory.koda.url` plus `memory.koda.headers`. Resolving `agent.modelAliases` for the role models is not part of this feature; `roles` are sent as given. US-001 only: a `costCapUsd` written in exponent notation (for example `1e-7`) fails the `String()` rule like any other bad value and needs no separate check. No existing source files need modification.

**Interface** — Add `kodaFlowConnection(config)` (the connection in "Credential and connection", or `undefined`) and `parseFlowSendInput(raw)` (the checks in "The request", returning the parsed input with every `dependsOn` defaulted to `[]`, or `{ errors: string[] }`). Export both functions and the shared types through `packages/nax/src/chat/flow/index.ts`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] kodaFlowConnection returns the url and headers when memory.koda.url is https://koda.example/api and memory.koda.headers holds Authorization: Bearer k.
[unit] kodaFlowConnection returns undefined when memory.koda.url is unset.
[unit] kodaFlowConnection returns undefined when memory.koda.headers has no authorization header in any letter case.
[unit] kodaFlowConnection returns undefined when the authorization header value is empty or whitespace.
[unit] kodaFlowConnection returns the connection when the header name is spelled AUTHORIZATION.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns the parsed input, with each missing dependsOn set to an empty array, for two valid features, two role strings and costCapUsd 5.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming features when the list is empty.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming features when it is not an array.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming the extra key when the input has a key other than features, roles and costCapUsd.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming roles.supervisor when roles has no supervisor.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming features when the list has 21 entries.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming the feature when a feature starts with -.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming the duplicate when two features share a name.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming the specPath when it contains a .. segment.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming the specPath when it does not end in .md.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming the specPath when it starts with /.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming the specPath when it contains a NUL character.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming the dependency when dependsOn names a feature listed later.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming dependsOn when it lists the same feature twice.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming the role when roles.reviewer contains a space.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming costCapUsd when it is 0.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming costCapUsd when it is 1000.01.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming costCapUsd when it is 1.23456.
[unit] parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming costCapUsd when it is the string "5".

routing.reasoning: Additive connection selector and pure validation across three small source files; selecting and preserving bearer credentials triggers the security override and strict three-session test isolation.

suggestedCriteria: kodaFlowConnection returns the same url and literal header values when memory.enabled is false, memory.provider is local and memory.koda.project is absent.
parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming features[0].dependsOn when the first feature depends on itself.
parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming the dependency when dependsOn names a feature absent from the list.
parseFlowSendInput returns errors naming specPath when it is empty or longer than 300 characters.
parseFlowSendInput returns the original specPath when it contains a harmless ./ segment.
parseFlowSendInput returns errors rather than throwing when raw is null, an array or a primitive.
parseFlowSendInput accepts costCapUsd 1000 and 1.2345.

userStories.title: Repository state and the koda call
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add deterministic repository preflight, GitHub remote normalization, koda branch checks and the authenticated flow-create client.

**Motivation** — The user wants one brainstorm to turn into ready PRs with as little of their attention as possible.

**Approach** — The repository:

All read from the chat's repository root before the card by `readFlowRepoState(repoRoot, specPaths)`,
which returns `{ ok: true, branch, sha, remoteUrl }` or `{ ok: false, message }`. The checks run in the order
below and the first failure is returned:

- the branch, from `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD`; a detached HEAD fails.
- the branch must pass `isPublishableBranch` (`packages/nax/src/utils/git.ts`); `main`, `master` and the
  empty name fail.
- the working tree must be clean (`isDirty` from `@/finish` returns false): nothing new is committed by
  this tool. Untracked files count, so a spec directory must be committed or ignored. When `isDirty` throws,
  the result is `{ ok: false, message: "[chat] could not read the repository state: <error message>" }`.
- the head sha, from `headSha` (`@/finish`); `null` (an unborn branch) fails with
  `[chat] the branch has no commits`.
- the remote URL, from `git remote get-url origin`, normalised to `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>`
  (lower-cased, no `.git` suffix, no trailing slash). Accepted forms: `https://github.com/o/r(.git)`,
  `git@github.com:o/r(.git)` and `ssh://git@github.com/o/r(.git)`. Any other host fails, because koda's
  `parseGitHubUrl` accepts GitHub HTTPS URLs only.
- every `specPath` must exist at `HEAD` (`git cat-file -e HEAD:<specPath>`); koda reads each spec at the
  sent sha and rejects a missing one only after the push.

A second pure check, `checkFlowBranch(branch, features)`, mirrors koda's branch rules and returns an error
message or `undefined`: the branch must match `^(?![-./])(?!.*\.\.)(?!.*//)(?!.*\.lock$)(?!.*/$)[A-Za-z0-9._/@+-]{1,255}$`,
and no feature at index 1 or later may be named so that `feat/<feature>` equals the branch.

`readFlowRepoState` reaches git only through `_flowRepoDeps = { git, isDirty, headSha }` (in
`flow-repo.ts`), whose defaults are `gitWithTimeout` (`@/utils/git`) and `isDirty`/`headSha` (`@/finish`);
tests replace these members. No raw spawn, so the `check-git-spawn-env` gate holds.

The body nax sends to `POST <memory.koda.url>/fleet/flows` (the client path argument is `fleet/flows`, with no leading slash, because `createKodaClient` joins the root and the path with `/`):

```json
{
  "remoteUrl": "https://github.com/nathapp-io/nax",
  "branch": "feat/nax-flow-send",
  "specSha": "<40-hex head sha>",
  "features": [
    { "feature": "nax-flow-send", "specPath": ".nax/features/nax-flow-send/spec.md", "dependsOn": [] },
    { "feature": "nax-flow-docs", "specPath": ".nax/features/nax-flow-docs/spec.md", "dependsOn": ["nax-flow-send"] }
  ],
  "roles": { "reviewer": "acp:codex", "supervisor": "acp:claude" },
  "costCapUsd": 5
}
```

POST the body above through `createKodaClient` (`@/memory`) built from the connection, with the new
constant `FLOW_KODA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (my call: koda's create calls GitHub for the branch
head and every spec file, so the memory client's 4 s deadline is too short).

201: koda created the flow. Return `{ kind: "created", id, state, url }`, requiring string `data.id`, `data.state` and `data.url`. 202: koda's approval policy is holding the create itself (`data` is koda's approval request summary). Return `{ kind: "held", requestId }` from string `data.id`. Any other 2xx status, or a 201 whose `data` lacks a string `id`, `state` or `url`, or a 202 whose `data` lacks a string `id`: `createKodaFlow` throws `NaxError` code `FLOW_KODA_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE`. Rethrow the client's `NaxError` unchanged.

Read-only integration contracts:
- `createKodaClient(input: CreateKodaClientInput): KodaClient` and `kodaStatusOf(error): number | undefined` — `packages/nax/src/memory/koda-http.ts`; `KodaResponse` is `{ status, data }`, where `data` is the envelope's `data`. A non-2xx status throws `NaxError` code `MEMORY_KODA_HTTP` whose message carries koda's `message`; transport failures throw `MEMORY_KODA_UNREACHABLE` or `MEMORY_KODA_TIMEOUT`.
- `isDirty(repoRoot)`, `headSha(repoRoot)`, `commitAndPush(repoRoot, branch, message, { skipCommit })` — `packages/nax/src/finish/commit.ts`, exported from `@/finish`.
- `isPublishableBranch(branch)` and `gitWithTimeout` — `packages/nax/src/utils/git.ts`.

**Scope** — In: Add `flow-repo.ts` and `flow-koda.ts`, export their public helpers, types, seam and timeout through the upstream flow barrel, and add corresponding unit tests. Out: Input parsing/credential selection is supplied by US-001; card, post-approval recheck, push, result formatting and user-facing HTTP error mapping belong to US-003; parent-chat composition belongs to US-004. Committing the spec files is not part of this tool; it requires a clean tree and never runs `git commit`. Supporting non-GitHub remotes (GitLab, self-hosted) is not part of this feature; koda accepts GitHub only. A config key for the koda request timeout is not part of this feature; it is the named constant `FLOW_KODA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`. Granting the koda agent `fleet.flow.create` is a koda-side setup step, not part of this feature; a 403 is reported as a koda error. Existing memory, finish, git and forge implementations remain read only.

**Interface** — Add `normalizeGitHubRemote(url)` (the HTTPS form or `null`), `readFlowRepoState(repoRoot, specPaths)` (the `{ ok }` union in "The repository"), `checkFlowBranch(branch, features)` and `createKodaFlow(connection, body)` (the POST through `createKodaClient` with `FLOW_KODA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, returning the 201 or 202 outcome, throwing `FLOW_KODA_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE` for any other answer, and rethrowing the client's `NaxError` unchanged). Git calls go through `_flowRepoDeps`. Export all of them from the flow barrel.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] normalizeGitHubRemote returns https://github.com/o/r for git@github.com:O/R.git.
[unit] normalizeGitHubRemote returns https://github.com/o/r for ssh://git@github.com/o/r.git.
[unit] normalizeGitHubRemote returns https://github.com/o/r for https://github.com/o/r/.
[unit] normalizeGitHubRemote returns null for https://gitlab.com/o/r.git.

[unit] With _flowRepoDeps.git answering branch feat/x, origin git@github.com:o/r.git and every cat-file successfully, _flowRepoDeps.isDirty false and _flowRepoDeps.headSha a 40-hex sha, readFlowRepoState returns { ok: true, branch: "feat/x", sha, remoteUrl: "https://github.com/o/r" }.
[unit] readFlowRepoState returns { ok: false, message: "[chat] nax-flow__send needs a checked-out branch" } when _flowRepoDeps.git fails symbolic-ref.
[unit] readFlowRepoState returns ok: false with a message naming main when the branch is main.
[unit] readFlowRepoState returns { ok: false, message: "[chat] commit or stash your changes before sending a flow" } when _flowRepoDeps.isDirty returns true.
[unit] readFlowRepoState returns ok: false with a message starting [chat] could not read the repository state:  when _flowRepoDeps.isDirty throws.
[unit] readFlowRepoState returns { ok: false, message: "[chat] the branch has no commits" } when _flowRepoDeps.headSha returns null.
[unit] readFlowRepoState returns { ok: false, message: "[chat] the repository has no origin remote" } when _flowRepoDeps.git fails remote get-url origin.
[unit] readFlowRepoState returns ok: false with a message naming https://gitlab.com/o/r.git when that is the origin.
[unit] readFlowRepoState returns ok: false with a message naming the path when _flowRepoDeps.git fails cat-file -e HEAD:<specPath> for one spec path.
[unit] readFlowRepoState returns the branch message, not the dirty-tree message, when the branch is main and the tree is dirty.
[unit] checkFlowBranch("feat/x", features) returns undefined for features x then y.
[unit] checkFlowBranch returns a message naming the branch for feat//x.
[unit] checkFlowBranch("feat/y", features) returns a message naming feature y when y is at index 1.

[unit] createKodaFlow with connection url https://koda.example/api posts the body to https://koda.example/api/fleet/flows through createKodaClient with timeout FLOW_KODA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, which equals 30000, and returns { kind: "created", id, state, url } for a 201 envelope.
[unit] createKodaFlow returns { kind: "held", requestId } for a 202 envelope whose data.id is the request id.
[unit] createKodaFlow rethrows the client's NaxError with code MEMORY_KODA_HTTP unchanged when koda answers 404.
[unit] createKodaFlow throws NaxError code FLOW_KODA_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE for a 200 answer.
[unit] createKodaFlow throws NaxError code FLOW_KODA_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE for a 201 answer whose data has no url.
[unit] readFlowRepoState returns ok: false with a [chat] message naming the branch when the checked-out branch is master or the empty name.

routing.reasoning: Two additive helper modules and a barrel extension reuse established git and koda clients with explicit sequential checks and response unions; authenticated bearer transport still mandates the security override's strict three-session isolation.

suggestedCriteria: normalizeGitHubRemote returns null for https://github.com.evil.example/o/r.git.
normalizeGitHubRemote returns https://github.com/o/r for https://github.com/O/R.git/.
checkFlowBranch returns a message naming the branch when it begins with -, . or /, contains .., ends with .lock or /, or exceeds 255 characters.
createKodaFlow throws FLOW_KODA_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE when a 202 response lacks a string data.id.
createKodaFlow throws FLOW_KODA_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE when a 201 response lacks a string data.id or data.state.
createKodaFlow rethrows the identical MEMORY_KODA_TIMEOUT or MEMORY_KODA_UNREACHABLE NaxError received from the client.

userStories.title: The nax-flow__send tool and its card
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose the static flow-send provider with mandatory host approval, a commit-bound push/create sequence and exact tool-result reporting.

**Motivation** — The user wants one brainstorm to turn into ready PRs with as little of their attention as possible.

**Approach** — A new static provider, id `nax-flow`, `stages: ["*"]`, one tool with local name `send` (qualified name `nax-flow__send`). Its run checks the input, the branch rules and the repository through US-001 and US-002 before the card. The input JSON schema has `additionalProperties: false`, requires `features`, `roles` and numeric `costCapUsd`, and describes the US-001 constraints; runtime parsing remains authoritative. Features have `feature`, `specPath` and optional `dependsOn`; roles have required reviewer and supervisor strings. Preserve the ordered features, defaulted dependsOn arrays, literal specPaths and unresolved role model strings.

The card:

One `HostApprovalCard` through `ChatAskController.requestHostApproval`, shown in **every** chat mode
including full (my call: `createHostJobs` skips its cards in full mode, so this tool must not reuse that
`approve` wrapper; pushing and creating a record in another system is outward-facing):

- `tool`: `nax-flow__send`
- `signal`: the tool run's `ctx.signal`, so a cancelled turn closes the card as a deny
- `summary`: `send a flow of <N> feature(s) to koda`
- `command`: `git push --set-upstream origin <branch>`
- `reason`, one string whose lines are joined with `\n`, in this order:
  1. `repo <remoteUrl> on branch <branch> at <sha first 8>`
  2. one line per feature: `<i>. <feature> (<specPath>)` followed by ` — after: <a>, <b>` when it has dependencies
  3. `reviewer <reviewer>, supervisor <supervisor>`
  4. `cost cap $<costCapUsd with 2 decimals>`
  5. `koda will ask you to approve this flow before anything billed starts`

A deny returns `[chat] the user declined sending the flow to koda; do not retry with different arguments
unless the user asks`, matching the jobs tools' wording.

After allow:

1. If `ctx.signal` is aborted, stop with nothing pushed. Then re-read the head sha and the working-tree state. If the sha differs from the carded one or the tree is
   dirty, fail with nothing pushed: the card described a different commit.
2. Push with `commitAndPush(repoRoot, branch, FLOW_PUSH_COMMIT_MESSAGE, { skipCommit: true })` (`@/finish`),
   which runs `git push --set-upstream origin <branch>`. `FLOW_PUSH_COMMIT_MESSAGE` (value `"chore: send flow to koda"`,
   exported from `flow-provider.ts` and the flow barrel) satisfies the required parameter; with `skipCommit` no
   commit is made.
3. POST the body above through `createKodaClient` (`@/memory`) built from the connection, with the new
   constant `FLOW_KODA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (my call: koda's create calls GitHub for the branch
   head and every spec file, so the memory client's 4 s deadline is too short).
4. Report the outcome (see Failure Handling for the error rows):
   - 201: koda created the flow. The result's first line is the JSON
     `{"flow":"<data.id>","state":"<data.state>","url":"<link>"}`, where `<link>` is the origin of
     `memory.koda.url` joined with koda's relative `data.url` (`/<project>/flows/<id>`); the second line is
     `koda will ask you to approve this flow before anything billed starts.`
   - 202: koda's approval policy is holding the create itself (`data` is koda's approval request summary).
     The result is
     `koda is holding the flow create for approval (request <data.id>); no flow exists until it is approved, and pushing new commits to the branch before then makes koda refuse it.`
   - any other 2xx status, or a 201 whose `data` lacks a string `id`, `state` or `url`, or a 202 whose `data`
     lacks a string `id`: `createKodaFlow` throws `NaxError` code `FLOW_KODA_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE`.

The link assumes koda's web UI is served from the same origin as its API (true for a koda deployment behind
one proxy); a koda under a path prefix would need the web root configured, which is out of scope.

The tool's seams live in `_flowProviderDeps = { readFlowRepoState, headSha, isDirty, commitAndPush,
createKodaFlow }` (in `flow-provider.ts`). `createFlowProvider(options: FlowProviderOptions)` takes
`{ repoRoot, connection, approve: (card: HostApprovalCard) => Promise<"allow" | "deny"> }`.

A spec review done in the chat is not sent as a claim: koda runs its own spec review.

Request body passed to `createKodaFlow(connection, body)`:
```json
{
  "remoteUrl": "https://github.com/nathapp-io/nax",
  "branch": "feat/nax-flow-send",
  "specSha": "<40-hex head sha>",
  "features": [
    { "feature": "nax-flow-send", "specPath": ".nax/features/nax-flow-send/spec.md", "dependsOn": [] },
    { "feature": "nax-flow-docs", "specPath": ".nax/features/nax-flow-docs/spec.md", "dependsOn": ["nax-flow-send"] }
  ],
  "roles": { "reviewer": "acp:codex", "supervisor": "acp:claude" },
  "costCapUsd": 5
}
```

Instructions:

The provider's instructions come from a new builder, `buildFlowInstructions()` in
`packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/flow-builder.ts`, exported through `@/prompts` (the prompt-builder rule).
They tell the brain: use the tool only when the user asks to hand specs to koda; the branch must be clean
and committed first, untracked files included; list features in dependency order; the user approves a card and then approves again in
koda.

Failure Handling:

Every failure is a tool result with `isError: true` and content starting `[chat] `; no failure throws out
of the tool.

The `send` run resolves to `ToolResult`, never a bare string: all text and JSON-line outcomes described here are its `content`; error results additionally have `isError: true`. Call `createKodaFlow(connection, body)` with the configured connection as the first argument and the assembled payload as the second argument.

| Condition | Behaviour |
|:--|:--|
| no koda connection (`memory.koda.url` unset or no non-empty `authorization` header) | the `nax-flow` provider is not offered |
| input fails a check in "The request" | error naming the field and the rule; no card, nothing pushed |
| detached HEAD | error `[chat] nax-flow__send needs a checked-out branch`; no card |
| branch is `main`, `master` or empty | error naming the branch; no card |
| working tree is dirty | error `[chat] commit or stash your changes before sending a flow`; no card |
| `git status` fails (`isDirty` throws) | error `[chat] could not read the repository state: <message>`; no card |
| unborn branch (`headSha` returns `null`) | error `[chat] the branch has no commits`; no card |
| branch fails koda's ref rule, or equals `feat/<feature>` for a feature at index 1 or later | error from `checkFlowBranch` naming the branch; no card |
| origin is missing (`git remote get-url origin` fails) | error `[chat] the repository has no origin remote`; no card |
| origin is not a GitHub remote | error naming the remote URL; no card |
| a `specPath` is absent at HEAD | error naming the path; no card |
| the user denies the card | the declined result in "The card"; nothing pushed |
| head sha changed or tree became dirty while the card was open | error `[chat] the branch changed while the card was open; nothing was pushed` |
| the turn is cancelled after allow (`ctx.signal` aborted) | error `[chat] the turn was cancelled; nothing was pushed` |
| `git push` fails | error with the push failure; koda is not called |
| koda answers non-2xx | error `[chat] koda did not create the flow (HTTP <status>): <koda message>; branch <branch> stays pushed`, where `<koda message>` is the client error's text after `answered <status>: ` |
| koda answers an unexpected 2xx or a body missing fields (`FLOW_KODA_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE`, or the client's `MEMORY_KODA_BAD_RESPONSE`) | error `[chat] koda answered unexpectedly: <message>; branch <branch> stays pushed` |
| any other error thrown inside the tool (a git rejection, a rejecting `approve`, an unclassified koda error) | error `[chat] flow send failed: <message>` |
| koda unreachable or timed out | error `[chat] koda could not be reached: <message>; branch <branch> stays pushed and no flow was created` |

**Scope** — In: Implement `flow-provider.ts`, its exported `FlowProviderOptions`, `_flowProviderDeps` and `FLOW_PUSH_COMMIT_MESSAGE`; extend the flow barrel; add the flow prompt builder and its @/prompts barrel export; add tool and builder unit tests. Out: US-001 owns parsing and connection selection; US-002 owns repository reading, branch validation and actual HTTP response classification; US-004 owns installing the provider into parent chat and ACP delivery. The missing-connection row is enforced by US-004 composition, not by inventing a new optional connection argument here. Committing the spec files is not part of this tool; it requires a clean tree and never runs `git commit`. Resolving `agent.modelAliases` for the role models is not part of this feature; `roles` are sent as given. Polling or watching the flow after creation is not part of this feature; the result carries the flow's link and the flow lives in koda. Configuring a koda web root separate from the API origin is not part of this feature; the flow link uses the origin of `memory.koda.url`.

**Interface** — `createFlowProvider(options: FlowProviderOptions)` takes `{ repoRoot, connection, approve: (card: HostApprovalCard) => Promise<"allow" | "deny"> }`. `HostApprovalCard { tool, summary, command?, reason, signal? }` and `ChatAskController.requestHostApproval(card): Promise<"allow" | "deny">` are from `packages/nax/src/chat/ask-controller.ts`. userStories.title: Offer the tool to the chat brain only
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Compose flow sending only into connected parent chats, deliver it to native and ACP brains, and preserve mandatory approval and subagent isolation.

**Motivation** — The user wants one brainstorm to turn into ready PRs with as little of their attention as possible.

**Approach** — Delivery:

- A new static provider, id `nax-flow`, `stages: ["*"]`, one tool with local name `send` (qualified name
  `nax-flow__send`).
- Composed only for the parent chat, in `createHostJobs`, and only when the connection is present. Its
  `approve` is `(card) => options.asks.requestHostApproval(card)`: a bound call (the method reads `this`) and
  not the jobs wrapper that auto-allows in full mode. `createHostJobs` gains a `providers` field, `[nax-jobs
  provider, nax-flow provider when present]`, and keeps `provider`. Because `createHostJobs` runs only when
  the chat has both `resources` and a nax entry, the flow tool needs both too. It is never added to
  `resources.toolProviders`, which is what subagents receive.
- `ACP_CHAT_PROVIDER_IDS` (`packages/nax/src/chat/acp/acp-tools.ts`) gains `nax-flow`, so the ACP brain
  receives it. `ACP_SUBAGENT_PROVIDER_IDS` (`acp-subagent-session.ts`) does not.
- `packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts` is at 599 lines against the 600-line limit. Its parent provider
  list (line 212) changes from `...(hostJobs ? [hostJobs.provider] : [])` to `...(hostJobs?.providers ?? [])`,
  a same-length edit, so the file stays at 599 lines.

Changed:

- `ACP_CHAT_PROVIDER_IDS`. Baseline (to locate the code only): `["nax-workflow", "nax-jobs", "nax-memory"]`.
  Target: `["nax-workflow", "nax-jobs", "nax-flow", "nax-memory"]`.
- `createHostJobs` (`packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts`). Target: its result adds
  `providers: readonly ToolProvider[]` (the jobs provider, then the flow provider when the connection is
  present) beside the unchanged `provider`; the chat host spreads `providers` where it spread `[provider]`.

In `createHostJobs`, compose `createFlowProvider` when `kodaFlowConnection(config)` returns a connection,
with `approve: (card) => options.asks.requestHostApproval(card)` (never the full-mode-skipping wrapper), and
return it in the new `providers` field after the jobs provider. Change the chat host's parent list to spread
`hostJobs?.providers`. Add `nax-flow` to `ACP_CHAT_PROVIDER_IDS`. Keep it out of `resources.toolProviders`
and `ACP_SUBAGENT_PROVIDER_IDS`. `chat-host.ts` stays at 599 lines.

Connection contract from US-001: The connection is present when `memory.koda.url` is set and `memory.koda.headers` has an `authorization` header (matched case-insensitively) with a non-empty value. `memory.enabled`, `memory.provider` and `memory.koda.project` play no part: koda resolves the repository from the remote URL. Empty or whitespace authorization is absent.

Existing assertions and harness changes:
- `packages/nax/test/unit/chat/acp/acp-tools.test.ts` — pins `ACP_CHAT_PROVIDER_IDS` to the three-id list; it must expect `["nax-workflow", "nax-jobs", "nax-flow", "nax-memory"]`.
- `packages/nax/test/helpers/chat-subagents.ts` — `SubagentHostOptions` gains optional `kodaConnection` (written into the config's `memory.koda` url and headers) and `naxEntry` (passed to `createChatHost`), so a subagent turn can run with the flow provider composed; existing callers pass neither and are unchanged. The new test lives in the host-subagents unit test file.

Seams:
- `[unit]` give `createChatHost` resources, a nax entry and a config whose `memory.koda.url` is set with an `authorization` header; start a native session; assert the open request's `toolProviders` contain `nax-flow` directly after `nax-jobs`.
- `[unit]` in `host-subagents.test.ts`, with the `chat-subagents.ts` harness given `kodaConnection` and `naxEntry`, start the host, send a turn that runs a subagent, and assert `nestedBackends[0].toolProviders` ids do not include `nax-flow`.
- `[unit]` with a koda connection, `_flowProviderDeps.readFlowRepoState` stubbed to `{ ok: true, branch: "feat/x", sha, remoteUrl }` and `_flowProviderDeps.headSha`/`isDirty` stubbed to the same sha and a clean tree, start the host in full mode and run its `nax-flow__send` tool with a valid input; assert the chat's `ChatAskController` has one pending host card whose `tool` is `nax-flow__send`.

**Scope** — In: Modify jobs-host.ts, the single chat-host.ts parent-list expression, acp-tools.ts, the existing jobs-host/chat-host-jobs/acp-tools/host-subagents unit tests and the shared chat-subagents harness. Import the upstream flow module through its barrel. Retain `provider`, existing jobs approval semantics, lifecycle/guard behavior and no-connection provider order. Out: US-001 owns connection parsing; US-002 owns repository and endpoint code; US-003 owns provider implementation and prompt text. Offering `nax-flow__send` to native or ACP subagents, or to `nax agents run`, is not part of this feature. Do not modify ACP_SUBAGENT_PROVIDER_IDS or add flow to shared resources.toolProviders. A new `koda` credential kind in the `nax auth` store, and `nax auth login koda`, are not part of this feature; the connection is `memory.koda.url` plus `memory.koda.headers`.

**Interface** — `createHostJobs` adds `providers: readonly ToolProvider[]` beside the unchanged `provider`. `createFlowProvider(options: FlowProviderOptions)` is supplied `{ repoRoot, connection, approve: (card: HostApprovalCard) => Promise<"allow" | "deny"> }`; pass `approve: (card) => options.asks.requestHostApproval(card)`. `ACP_CHAT_PROVIDER_IDS` becomes `["nax-workflow", "nax-jobs", "nax-flow", "nax-memory"]`; `ACP_SUBAGENT_PROVIDER_IDS` is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] createChatHost with resources, a nax entry and a koda connection passes an open request whose toolProviders contain nax-flow directly after nax-jobs.
[unit] createChatHost with resources and a nax entry but no memory.koda block passes toolProviders without nax-flow.
[unit] In host-subagents.test.ts, with the chat-subagents.ts harness given kodaConnection and naxEntry, a subagent turn's nestedBackends[0].toolProviders ids do not include nax-flow.

[unit] With a koda connection, the repository deps stubbed to a clean feat/x and the session in full mode, running the host's nax-flow__send with a valid input leaves one pending host card with tool nax-flow__send on the chat's ChatAskController.
[unit] createHostJobs with a koda connection returns providers whose ids are ["nax-jobs", "nax-flow"], and ["nax-jobs"] without one.
[unit] ACP_CHAT_PROVIDER_IDS equals ["nax-workflow", "nax-jobs", "nax-flow", "nax-memory"].
[unit] chatAcpTools given the nax-flow provider with default options returns a tool named nax-flow__send.
[unit] createHostJobs does not offer the nax-flow provider when memory.koda.url is unset or memory.koda.headers lacks a non-empty, non-whitespace authorization header matched case-insensitively.
[unit] createHostJobs returns provider identical to providers[0] with and without a koda connection, preserving the existing single-provider access for callers that still read provider.

routing.reasoning: Existing composition and ACP allow-list mechanisms need only localized wiring plus an optional harness extension, not a new abstraction; parent/subagent access isolation and mandatory full-mode approval require the security override's three-session isolation.

suggestedCriteria: createChatHost does not offer nax-flow when a koda connection exists but resources or naxEntry is absent.
When a connected chat starts in guarded mode, running nax-flow__send with valid input leaves exactly one pending host approval card.
When a connected host opens an ACP subagent, the delivered ACP tools do not contain nax-flow__send.
When a connected host is composed, resources.toolProviders retains its original provider ids and order.

The new test lives in the host-subagents unit test file.

analysis:
Repository exploration: codebase-memory MCP is not exposed in this session, so navigation used direct reads and text searches rooted at /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax-flow-send. The checked-in source spec is .nax/features/nax-flow-send/spec.md:1. This is an additive enhancement to the Bun/TypeScript @nathapp/nax package, not a greenfield project and not a cross-package auth change. The chat/flow directory does not exist yet. Implement exactly US-001 -> US-002 -> US-003 -> US-004, all with workdir packages/nax.

Architecture and conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:15 identifies the injectable _deps, NaxError, constant and barrel conventions; docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:145 gives the 600-line source hard limit, 400-line soft limit, function-size guidance and test patterns. Use Bun-native runtime facilities, strict unknown-input validation, discriminated result unions, public module barrels and named constants. Tests use bun:test, existing @test/helpers, restored mutable dependency seams and event-driven waits rather than sleeps or live git/network calls. Source prompt text must live in src/prompts/builders and be consumed through @/prompts (packages/nax/src/prompts/index.ts:1). No nax-ai, nax-agent or nax-agent-acp source changes, new dependency, config migration, version bump or release is needed. All stories touch credential use, authenticated requests, approvals or provider access boundaries; use three-session-tdd under the security override. The bound method closure and separation of outward-facing approval from chat permission modes are intentional security decisions.

US-001 findings: packages/nax/src/config/schemas-memory.ts:110 defines MemoryKodaConfigSchema with optional url and project and literal header strings; :120 defines memory.enabled/provider and :143 exposes memoryConfigOf for optional memory config. Flow connectivity must read only url plus a case-insensitive, non-whitespace authorization value, independently of enabled, provider or project. The existing memory-provider validation requires project only when memory.provider is koda (schemas-memory.ts:186); do not import that requirement into flow availability. packages/nax/src/config/global-only-keys.ts:10 and :32 already protect koda url/headers against project-layer redirection; packages/nax/src/config/dotenv.ts:118 preserves memory.koda.headers literally. packages/nax/src/memory/koda-http.ts:57 defines CreateKodaClientInput with url, readonly headers and timeoutMs. Reuse these shapes without introducing a second credential store or changing config schema. Add flow-input.ts, flow-connection.ts and a flow barrel; the parser must enforce the exact feature, path, dependency, role and numeric constraints without coercing strings or normalizing paths/models. Include parser/connection tests under test/unit/chat/flow.

US-002 findings: packages/nax/src/finish/commit.ts:29 implements isDirty using git status --porcelain, including untracked files and throwing FINISH_GIT_STATUS_FAILED on nonzero status; :42 returns headSha or null. packages/nax/src/utils/git.ts:7 re-exports gitWithTimeout and :26 implements isPublishableBranch protecting empty/main/master. flow-repo.ts should use only _flowRepoDeps = { git, isDirty, headSha }, with git argv omitting the git executable. Read branch, publishability, cleanliness, sha, origin and committed specs sequentially; first failure wins. packages/nax/src/forge/detect.ts:53 is the existing origin-read precedent, but its :24 host classification intentionally accepts enterprise forge variants; do not reuse that permissiveness for flow's github.com-only normalizer. Preserve specPath byte-for-byte into git cat-file and the request. checkFlowBranch is a separate pure check after repository success and before the card.

HTTP integration: packages/nax/src/memory/koda-http.ts:96 concatenates the root and path with '/', so post('fleet/flows', body), never post('/fleet/flows', body). :41 exposes the existing 4000ms memory deadline; do not change it. Build the flow client with FLOW_KODA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000. :43 defines KodaResponse as transport status plus the envelope's unknown data, :249 unwraps data, :278 preserves NaxError identity, :304 creates the client and :312 exposes kodaStatusOf using context.status. Its timeout covers the full response and its header redaction includes bearer tokens (koda-http.ts:121, :161, :269). packages/nax/src/memory/index.ts:16 already exports the client and status helper through @/memory. Add flow-koda.ts using that public boundary and a NaxError FLOW_KODA_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE for unexpected 2xx or missing required string fields; do not swallow/re-wrap client errors. packages/nax/src/errors.ts:7 re-exports the existing extensible NaxError. Tests can drive the real client through _kodaClientDeps.fetch, inspecting exact URL/body/headers and timeout behavior without real network calls. Existing memory/koda-http.test.ts:67, :169, :233 and :280 cover request building, response errors, timeouts and redaction and are regression references, not files to rewrite.

US-003 findings: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-provider.ts:142 shows the static ToolProvider shape (id, kind, stages, async instructions/tools) and ProviderTool inputSchema/run conventions. :17 shows the mutable collaborator seam; :99 shows additionalProperties:false. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/chain-tools.ts:140 joins approval reasons with newlines, and :122 builds ToolResult errors. packages/nax/src/chat/ask-controller.ts:25 defines HostApprovalCard; :113 requestHostApproval creates one pending host card regardless of mode, denies an already-aborted signal and hooks abort cleanup. That method uses this, so callers must preserve binding. Flow needs an explicit try/catch across the entire run so validation, git, approval rejections and HTTP failures never escape as thrown tool errors; every error is isError:true with [chat] prefix. Validate input, read repository, check koda's ref rule, show one card, deny without side effects, then check abort and re-read sha/dirty before pushing. The card approves a specific commit, not billed execution. A later branch race after re-check is not eliminated atomically; send the carded sha and let koda remain authoritative. Do not add retries: push may already have happened and the endpoint has externally visible effects.

Push and outcomes: packages/nax/src/finish/commit.ts:118 takes the required message argument and :124 bypasses committing with skipCommit:true; :128 pushes --set-upstream origin branch with its existing 120000ms push deadline. _flowProviderDeps must expose repository read, sha, dirty, push and create collaborators. Export FLOW_PUSH_COMMIT_MESSAGE = 'chore: send flow to koda' and the provider from the flow barrel. buildFlowInstructions belongs in a new prompts/builders/flow-builder.ts and is exported from prompts/index.ts beside existing builders (workflow-builder.ts:56 is the fixed jobs-instruction precedent). Treat 201 created and 202 held separately; a held request has no flow yet. Build the 201 link from the API origin plus the relative returned UI URL, not the /api root. No chat review claim is sent. Error mapping must distinguish HTTP status (strip the client's 'answered <status>: ' prefix), unexpected response/bad JSON, unreachable/timeout and generic failure. The specified unreachable/timeout text asserts no flow was created, though transport timeout can leave remote outcome uncertain; preserve the specified contract and do not invent polling or retries. Tests belong in flow-provider.test.ts and prompts/builders/flow-builder.test.ts, with every failure-table row represented in matching-story criteria.

US-004 findings: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts:27 is the parent-only composition boundary, :49 auto-allows jobs cards in full mode and :54 constructs the existing jobs provider. Retain that jobs behavior and provider field unchanged; add providers:readonly ToolProvider[] ordered [jobs, optional flow], using kodaFlowConnection(config) and a separate approve:(card)=>options.asks.requestHostApproval(card). packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:169 only calls createHostJobs when both resources and naxEntry exist. :194 passes resources.toolProviders directly to createSubagentRuns, while :212 builds the parent provider list. Replace only ...(hostJobs ? [hostJobs.provider] : []) with ...(hostJobs?.providers ?? []) at :212; the verified file has 599 lines and must remain at 599. Never mutate resources.toolProviders. packages/nax/src/chat/acp/acp-tools.ts:18 currently allows workflow/jobs/memory and :46 filters supplied providers through the default chat allow-list; add nax-flow between jobs and memory. packages/nax/src/chat/acp/acp-subagent-session.ts:46 has the separate workflow/memory subagent allow-list and :52 derives the unattended list; neither gains flow. The parent's ACP mapper already forwards tools with approval:'never' (acp-tools.test.ts:77), so the provider's own mandatory host card is the essential approval boundary.

Dependents and regression path: createHostJobs is exported at packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/index.ts:14, consumed by chat-host.ts:40, and directly exercised by test/unit/chat/jobs/jobs-host.test.ts:49 and test/unit/chat/chat-host-chain.test.ts:74. Keeping provider plus all lifecycle/guard fields is backward compatible for those callers. Existing jobs-host.test.ts:85 pins full-mode bypass, :97 guarded cards and :109 dynamic mode changes; do not change these expectations when adding flow. test/unit/chat/chat-host-jobs.test.ts:39 provides an open-request capture fixture; :143 pins no-connection provider order, :157 covers resources-only and :174 entry-only hosts. Extend the fixture with connection input and add positive ordering, missing-connection and full-mode mandatory-card cases while preserving current jobs behavior. test/unit/chat/acp/acp-tools.test.ts:61 explicitly pins the old three-id list and must change to the four-id target; add delivery of nax-flow__send without changing unrelated filtered-provider tests. test/unit/chat/host-subagents.test.ts:104 captures nested backend provider ids. test/helpers/chat-subagents.ts:214 defines SubagentHostOptions, :314 constructs config and :468 calls createChatHost; add optional kodaConnection and naxEntry only, defaulting to existing behavior, then exercise a real scripted subagent turn with flow composed and assert nestedBackends[0] excludes it. The harness already records native/ACP backend and provider calls and restores seams in dispose (chat-subagents.ts:304, :438, :512).

Delivery and risk summary: additive helpers first, then git/HTTP integration, then provider/mandatory card and prompt, finally parent-only composition and ACP exposure. New flow module files and their tests are outputs; previously created flow/index.ts is upstream context for later stories, not a newly authored output again. No existing production code changes until US-003's prompts barrel and US-004's three integration files. Primary risks are accidental enabling via memory provider/project settings, credential leakage or re-expansion, permissive remote parsing, altered spec paths, incorrect decimal coercion, approval bypass in full mode, lost method binding, stale-card pushes, misclassifying 202 as a flow, lost HTTP status/cause information, and native/ACP subagent leakage. Preserve every exact user-facing failure message and don't introduce behavior outside the spec. Validation is package scoped (targeted bun test <path> --timeout=30000; pipeline owns typecheck/lint/tests); never use bare bun test or bun run nax, and never run coverage inside NAX_SANDBOXED=1. This PRD itself does not require running application tests. Koda's live endpoint is external and remains the final validator and billed-start approver; granting fleet.flow.create is an operator setup step, not a code migration.

Refine audit: manually enumerated and matched all 76 explicitly stated spec acceptance criteria, in story order (US-001: 24; US-002: 22; US-003: 23; US-004: 7), preserving the unchanged-client-error qualifier, no-side-effect clauses, denial retry restriction, defaulted dependencies, exact message punctuation, pending-create warning and default-options/full-mode qualifiers. The extra failure-table criteria remain in their matching stories; all four stories have negative cases. Tool outcomes are ToolResult objects, so string-output criteria now explicitly assert content, including the created and held terminal periods; createKodaFlow receives connection first and body second. All 10 feature-level exclusions remain verbatim and binding dependencies are unchanged. US-004 context now includes the upstream flow barrel, completing its five spec-recommended source files; the helper remains described as a modification, not a new output. US-002 and US-004 complexity is medium because they reuse existing mechanisms, while security-critical credential, authenticated transport and approval/access-boundary work still requires three-session-tdd. US-004 now explicitly protects the existing provider field identity and jobs-only full-mode approval bypass; flow remains carded in full mode. These regression anchors match packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts:27-34 and :49-53, and its existing unit tests at test/unit/chat/jobs/jobs-host.test.ts:83-107. No acceptance criteria were removed or reassigned.
outOfScope:
A new `koda` credential kind in the `nax auth` store, and `nax auth login koda`, are not part of this
  feature; the connection is `memory.koda.url` plus `memory.koda.headers`.
Resolving `agent.modelAliases` for the role models is not part of this feature; `roles` are sent as given.
Committing the spec files is not part of this tool; it requires a clean tree and never runs `git commit`.
Supporting non-GitHub remotes (GitLab, self-hosted) is not part of this feature; koda accepts GitHub only.

Polling or watching the flow after creation is not part of this feature; the result carries the flow's
  link and the flow lives in koda.

A config key for the koda request timeout is not part of this feature; it is the named constant
  `FLOW_KODA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`.
Offering `nax-flow__send` to native or ACP subagents, or to `nax agents run`, is not part of this feature.
US-001 only: a `costCapUsd` written in exponent notation (for example `1e-7`) fails the `String()` rule like any other bad value and needs no separate check.

Configuring a koda web root separate from the API origin is not part of this feature; the flow link uses
  the origin of `memory.koda.url`.

Granting the koda agent `fleet.flow.create` is a koda-side setup step, not part of this feature; a 403
  is reported as a koda error.
